title: Graduated region hedging with tenant-preserving variant escape hatches
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a routing policy that balances tenant affinity to Dedicated capacity while safely using hosted capacity as a backfill during transient shortages without regressing per-tenant quality or SLOs. Existing tickets cover many heuristics for spillover and affinity; this proposal focuses on a graduated hedging strategy plus a set of explicit 'escape hatches' (variant demotion and token-escrow) to limit customer impact and provide deterministic rollback points.

Goals:
- Preserve latency and QoE for high-priority tenants on Dedicated while avoiding large global disruption during regional pressure.
- Allow staged, reversible migration to hosted variants with bounded risk to token cost and output quality.
- Provide clear observability and runbook actions for operators.

Summary of proposal:
- Introduce a 4-state policy state machine applied per-tenant-per-region: NORMAL -> HEDGED -> SOFT_BACKFILL -> EMERGENCY_BACKFILL.
- Region score composed from: available_capacity_pct (40%), p95_latency_headroom (30%), tenant_priority_affinity (20%), model_variant_quality_delta (10%). Tunable weights.
- Graduated hedging: when score breaches warning threshold, traffic is probabilistically steered (5% -> 20% -> 60%) to hosted-compatible model variants rather than instant full spillover. Steering respects tenant token reservations and honors tenant-specific deny-lists.
- Escape hatches: (1) Variant-demote path with synchronous quality gate and automatic rollback on quality regressions; (2) Token-escrow: short-lived soft throttle that preserves per-tenant reserved tokens during emergency backfill windows; (3) Circuit-breaker with cooldown and manual override.
- Safety escrow lanes: reserve a small Dedicated buffer (configurable per-tier) to handle bursty requests while hedging to hosted.

Trade-offs considered:
- More conservative (full-reserve) approach reduces hosted cost efficiency but guarantees tenant isolation — rejected because it blocks efficient utilization.
- Aggressive probabilistic steering is faster to relieve pressure but increases quality variance — we choose graduated steps with quality checks to balance speed vs risk.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag behind per-tenant gate.
2) Canary for internal tenants and 10 low-risk external tenants (2 weeks).
3) Gradual expansion: 2% tenants -> 25% tenants -> all tenants over 6 weeks, with kill-switch.

QA & Validation:
- Synthetic traffic tests (region pressure emulator) to verify state transitions and steering percentages.
- Chaos tests that simulate Dedicated node loss and noisy neighbors.
- Blind-quality evals on a cross-section of prompts comparing Dedicated vs hosted variants under hedged steering.

Observability & Metrics needed:
- per-tenant and per-region: p95_latency, error_rate, spillover_rate, percent_hosted_traffic, variant_quality_delta (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval proxy), token_cost_delta, SLA_violation_count.
- Alerts: spillover_rate > 15% for > 10m, variant_quality_delta > threshold for > 5m, circuit-breaker opened.

Runbook summary (operator actions):
- If spillover_rate rises unexpectedly: check region_score signals, verify Dedicated node metrics, engage capacity-burst plan.
- If variant quality regression observed: immediately flip to NORMAL state for affected tenants and open incident.
- For EMERGENCY_BACKFILL: notify customer success and throttle non-critical low-tier tenants using token-escrow.

Links to artifacts and drafts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SMART-ROUTING-V2 (draft)
- Architecture diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/sr-v2-arch (diagram-v3.png)
- PR (routing engine changes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2187
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/sr2/region-hedge-overview

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Weight tuning: initial weights above are provisional — propose A/B search via canary.
- Token-escrow policy: should it be percentage-based or absolute tokens? (proposal: start percentage-based per-tier).
- Should we expose tenant-level overrides in Console or keep as API-only? (PM to decide).
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant state machine implemented and feature-flagged
Region score computed in routing layer and surfaced to dashboards
Graduated steering percentages respected under regional pressure tests
Escape hatch flows (variant-demote, token-escrow, circuit-breaker) implemented and exercised in QA
Monitoring and alerts for the key metrics provisioned
Canary rollout executed with no >1% increase in P95 for canary tenants
implementation_notes: Routing engine: add region_score hook and decision layer (java/kotlin module)
Serving runtime: ensure hosted-compatible model variants registered with quality fingerprints
Control plane: per-tenant flags and safety-escrow config stored in tenant-config service
Console: add tenant routing page to show current state and allow read-only view initially
Billing: add metric to track hosted token delta during canary for cost analysis
